key_finding: At 150-slide scale (vs the earlier 20-slide scale where all models were statistically indistinguishable, mean 0.625-0.708), a genuine performance separation emerges. CNN-MIL is clearly weakest (mean 0.893, std 0.094), particularly struggling on Fold 1 (0.730). Foundation-MIL (0.962 ± 0.045) and Fusion-MIL (0.966 ± 0.041) are close, with Fusion marginally ahead but within overlapping variance -- the two are not confidently distinguishable from each other, only from CNN-MIL. This is directionally consistent with the fusion hypothesis but the CNN-vs-foundation-pathway gap is the more robust finding here.
caveat: 150 slides is a documented subset (not the full 270-slide official CAMELYON16 training set). Val folds are ~37-38 slides each -- much more robust than the earlier 20-slide experiment, but final generalization should still be confirmed on a held-out test set before any deployment claim.
